name: MITIGATTI (GATTI)
description: Mitigatti (also known as Gatti) is a traditional Italian trick-taking game played with a Tarot deck (Tarocchi). Popular in the Piedmont and Liguria regions, it is a complex game involving 78 cards, including 21 trumps and the Joker-like 'Matto'. It features a unique 'Bargaining' phase where players can negotiate to end a hand early based on their card strength, and scoring is based on both captured tricks and specific card combinations (declarations).

content.text: Mitigatti (also known as Gatti) is a traditional Italian trick-taking game played with a Tarot deck (Tarocchi). Popular in the Piedmont and Liguria regions, it is a complex game involving 78 cards, including 21 trumps and the Joker-like 'Matto'. It features a unique 'Bargaining' phase where players can negotiate to end a hand early based on their card strength, and scoring is based on both captured tricks and specific card combinations (declarations).
Dates back centuries to the evolution of Tarot games in Northern Italy. It is closely related to 'Tarocchini' and 'Minchiate'.

78-card Italian-suited tarot pack. The Nice source describes the older Piedmontese / Marseille-style structure while noting that local players had largely switched to French-suited tarot cards by the early twentieth century.
